category_title: Struggling and reluctant middle school learners in intervention language arts
minimal_context: The student is participating in a Reading and Discussion rotation where they are asked to read assigned pages from the novel 'Stargirl' out loud to the group.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright, it's time for our Reading and Discussion rotation. We are going to take turns reading the assigned pages from 'Stargirl' out loud to the group.

STUDENT: (Whispers to a peer) I'm not reading this.

TUTOR: Jesse, please start us off by reading the first page out loud.

STUDENT: I didn't get to practice it by myself first. I'm not doing it.

TUTOR: Just give it a try. Read the first paragraph for us.

STUDENT: (Puts head down on the desk, refusing to work) No. I'm not reading out loud in front of everyone.

options.A: Adjust the ratio of lower-level to higher-level questions based on the student's current reading level.
options.B: Create caring, respectful relationships with the student during the reading and discussion rotation.
options.C: Address the student's avoidance strategies as compensations rather than refusals to comply with the reading task.
options.D: Pre-plan open-ended questions that are not designed for one correct interpretation of the assigned text.
